author: w. n. barry
title: Late home run secures 7-6 win for Samford baseball over Jacksonville State - Jefferson Reporter
text:
Samford University’s baseball team earned a 7-6 victory against Jacksonville State on March 17, after freshman Eddie Marshall hit a two-run home run in the eighth inning at Rudy Abbott Field at Jim Case Stadium.
The win brings Samford’s season record to 8-11, while Jacksonville State falls to 17-4. The game was closely contested, with both teams exchanging leads before Samford secured the win in the final innings.
“This was a really good college baseball game where we had some guys really clutch up down the stretch,” Samford head coach Tony David said. “Jax State has a really good baseball team. It’s hard to put into words how clutch Marshall has been at the end of games with the long ball. He drove that ball out opposite field against an outstanding closer.”
Samford’s offense was led by Jeffrey Ince, who went 3-for-5 with two doubles and an RBI, and Jake Souders, who contributed a home run and three RBI. Cade Carr also hit a solo home run early in the game. On the mound, John Malone pitched over two innings allowing just one hit to earn the win, while Zak Spurrier closed out the game with four strikeouts for his third save of the season.
David praised his pitching staff after the game: “Berry was great to get things going in the mound and we had several guys throw well,” he said. “But Spurrier was the story and was electric to finish it. We got him going a little and showed emotion that is rare for him. This was a great way to finish off the pre-season. We have confidence in this group at the plate. Today was a good step forward. Looking forward to starting up league play.”
Jacksonville State took its largest lead after scoring five runs in the fourth inning but could not hold off Samford’s late rally. The Bulldogs will begin Southern Conference play this weekend with a three-game series at Western Carolina.
